import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Drop rows with missing income values, as they are crucial for this plot
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Feature Engineering: Create new insightful columns
# 1. Total spending on main product categories
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# 2. Total number of children/dependents at home
df['Dependents'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# 3. Customer Age
current_year = pd.to_datetime('today').year
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']

# Filter out extreme outliers for a clearer visualization
df_plot = df[(df['Income'] < 200000) & (df['Age'] < 90)].copy()

# Convert 'Dependents' to a categorical type for better plotting with discrete colors
df_plot['Dependents'] = df_plot['Dependents'].astype('category')


# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatter plot (bubble chart)
# This plot shows the relationship between Income and Spending,
# with point color representing the number of dependents and
# point size representing the customer's age.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_plot,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Dependents',
    size='Age',
    sizes=(30, 300),
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title
ax.set_title(
    'Customer Spending by Income, Segmented by Dependents and Age',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=20
)

# Set informative axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the tick labels on both axes for better readability (e.g., $60,000)
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Improve the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate handles and labels for 'hue' and 'size'
hue_title = 'Dependents'
size_title = 'Age'
num_dependents_levels = len(df_plot['Dependents'].cat.categories)

# Create two separate legends for clarity
legend1 = ax.legend(
    handles[1:num_dependents_levels + 1],
    labels[1:num_dependents_levels + 1],
    title=hue_title,
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11'
)
ax.add_artist(legend1) # Add the first legend back to the plot

legend2 = ax.legend(
    handles[num_dependents_levels + 2:],
    labels[num_dependents_levels + 2:],
    title=size_title,
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6),
    loc='upper left',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11'
)

# Adjust plot layout to make room for labels and title
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust right margin for legends

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
